title: group/verb dispatch seam in queen-bee + generic bee-parity --cmd-check arm (arbitrary command, stdout+exit+tree diff)
action: Build the two seams every later ledger cell depends on, and NOTHING else -- no ledger group is ported here. (1) DISPATCH: crates/queen-bee/src/main.rs today is a flat single-word match (main.rs:20-36). Add a group/verb layer beside it: `queen-bee <group> <verb> [flags]` resolves through a registration table so a new group is one registration, not a main.rs rewrite. Flag parsing, unknown-flag refusal text, and missing-required-flag refusal text must reproduce the mjs wording byte-for-byte -- REVIEW CORRECTION -- the oracle is NOT bee-core/src/validate_args.rs. packages/bee/lib/validate-args.mjs:90 disclaims it in its own comment (`if (!propSchema) continue; // unknown-flag rejection is the dispatcher's own concern`). The real producer is packages/bee/bee.mjs:7186-7188, `${commandName.split('.').join(' ')}: unknown flag --${flagName} (known: ${known}).`, built from the REGISTRY entry's parameters.properties -- so the refusal text cannot be produced at all without a resolvable registry (see obligation B). The quoted string was independently reproduced from that generator over command-registry.mjs:501-509 and is byte-exact. Reuse bee-core::registry for the command-def bridge rather than hardcoding a second list (D7 names command-registry.mjs as the enumeration authority). (2) PARITY: crates/bee-parity today only knows --status-check. Add a generic --cmd-check arm following the check_one_leg shape at bee-parity/src/main.rs:343-438: it takes an argv scenario list, runs the SAME argv on both runtimes over cloned golden fixtures (runner::Runtime::Mjs spawns node <bee.mjs>, Runtime::QueenBee spawns the binary), and diffs the outputs plus the resulting .bee/ + docs/ file tree via differ::diff_legs. Every scenario also runs the seeded-mutation negative control (main.rs:427-432) -- a rig reporting zero diff on real divergence is untrusted and this cell is red. Fixtures come from queen-bench --generate, never hand-authored. THREE ADVISOR-FOUND OBLIGATIONS, all mandatory, all in THIS cell because every later cell inherits the surface. (a) STDERR IS IN THE DIFF SURFACE. runner::RunResult today captures stdout + exit code only (crates/bee-parity/src/runner.rs:118-124). Several contracts later cells must prove are stderr-ONLY: the reviews fail-open warning (packages/bee/lib/reviews.mjs:130) and the rejection text whose JS regex-literal spelling rpl-3 is obligated to reproduce (packages/bee/lib/decisions.mjs:280-283). Capture stderr in RunResult and diff it, or rpl-3's and rpl-7's obligations are unprovable and the proof is theater. (b) NONDETERMINISM NORMALIZATION MUST ASSERT FORMAT, NOT JUST MASK. Every write verb stamps wall-clock and randomness with no injection seam -- crypto.randomUUID()/toISOString() at packages/bee/lib/decisions.mjs:320-322, reviews.mjs:46,348, backlog.mjs:284, and tempfile suffixes at decisions.mjs:220 -- so a raw byte-diff can NEVER match on a write verb. Extend crates/bee-parity/src/normalize.rs so each volatile field is masked AND its shape asserted on BOTH sides: the ISO timestamp must be the 3-digit-millisecond Z form JS toISOString() emits (chrono has RFC3339 variants that differ), and the id must be UUID-v4 shaped. A mask without a shape assertion silently hides real drift and is itself a red. Document the volatile-field list as a deny-by-default allowlist: a field is masked only if it is named, so a new unmasked volatile field fails loudly instead of passing quietly. (c) NUMERIC-STRING KEY ORDER. JS JSON.stringify reorders integer-like object keys ascending while serde_json preserve_order keeps insertion order; any ledger object carrying numeric-string keys diverges despite preserve_order. Add one scenario whose payload has numeric-string keys and prove the two runtimes still agree, or record in the worker block that no ledger object can carry such keys, with the evidence. Register at least two smoke scenarios that pass today (--help --json, an unknown-group refusal) so the arm is proven live, not merely compiled. FOUR REVIEW-FOUND OBLIGATIONS, all mandatory, all here because every later cell inherits this surface. (A) THE VERIFY MUST DISCRIMINATE. A bare --cmd-check exits 0 on this cell's own smoke scenarios alone, so a later worker who registers nothing still gets green. Add `--cmd-check --group <name>`, which runs only that group's scenarios and EXITS NON-ZERO when the group has registered zero, plus `--cmd-check --all`. Print the registered-scenario count per group so the number is visible in the verify output. (B) THE REGISTRY IS ABSENT FROM THE FIXTURE, WHICH BREAKS THIS CELL'S OWN MUST-HAVE. bee-core's load_registry (crates/bee-core/src/registry.rs:112) resolves store-root-relative paths -- `.bee/cache/command-registry.json` and `.bee/bin/lib/command-registry.mjs` (crates/queen-bee/src/hooks/write_guard.rs:1254-1255) -- and crates/queen-bench/src/fixture.rs writes NEITHER, so load_registry errors on every scenario and both smoke scenarios plus the refusal-text truth are unachievable. Seed both files into the cmd-check fixture. This is safe for the tree diff precisely because `.bee/cache` is already in EXCLUDED_PREFIXES (crates/bee-parity/src/differ.rs:28) -- the point is to make the two legs resolve the SAME registry, not to diff it. (C) THE NEGATIVE CONTROL CANNOT FIRE FOR ANY LEDGER COMMAND AS BUILT. crates/bee-parity/src/mutate.rs:25-34 seed_mutation flips `.bee/state.json`'s phase and refuses unless that file byte-equals FIXTURE_STATE_BODY (mutate.rs:16); main.rs:428-432 then errors if the flip produced no stdout diff. No ledger verb -- intent show, capture count, decisions active, backlog counts, reviews list, feedback rank -- prints phase, so EVERY ledger scenario would fail its own negative control. Make the mutation target per-scenario: each scenario declares the store it actually reads, and seed_mutation perturbs THAT. A scenario with no declared mutation target is refused at registration, not silently skipped. (D) SCOPE THE FIXTURE PROHIBITION HONESTLY. `queen-bench --generate` produces only what `status` needed and its ledger content is monotone filler: every decisions row is type `decide` with an identical date, no tags and no supersede/redact rows (fixture.rs:287); every backlog row is type `proposal` (fixture.rs:296); ids are zero-padded so byte order equals numeric order; and there is no capture queue, no intent store, no decisions-archive, no docs/decisions/index.md, no docs/backlog.md and no learnings tree. Keep `--generate` as the authority for the BASELINE store -- never hand-author that -- but explicitly permit and require PER-SCENARIO SEEDING on the clone, so a scenario can add the superseded, redacted, non-ASCII, tagged, dual-schema and non-zero-padded rows its assertion actually needs. Say this in the arm's own docs; without it every later cell's edge scenarios are non-discriminating against a monotone store. ALSO IN SCOPE HERE: the per-group unknown-VERB usage fallback (packages/bee/bee.mjs:6586-6609 GROUP_USAGE_FALLBACKS) -- this cell owns the shared mechanism; each group cell asserts its own fallback line.

truths: cargo run --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p bee-parity -- --cmd-check --all runs and reports every registered scenario clean, with the scenario argv printed per line
the seeded-mutation negative control fires for every scenario: a deliberately corrupted rust output IS reported as a diff, and the control covers stderr as well as stdout
runner::RunResult captures stderr and differ::diff_legs diffs it, proven by a scenario whose only difference would be on stderr
every masked volatile field also has its SHAPE asserted on both sides (ISO 3-digit-ms Z form, UUID-v4 form), proven by a negative control that changes only the shape and is still caught
the volatile-field list is deny-by-default: an unnamed volatile field fails the diff rather than passing quietly, proven by a test adding one
the numeric-string-key question is settled either by a passing scenario or by a worker-block statement with evidence that no ledger object can carry such keys
the group registration surface is proven by a TEST, not a comment: a test registers a throwaway group and asserts it is dispatchable and enumerable with no edit to main.rs
unknown-flag and missing-required-flag refusal text is byte-identical to mjs for at least one real command, proven by a --cmd-check scenario
`--cmd-check --group <name>` exits NON-ZERO for a group with zero registered scenarios, and prints the registered count per group
the command registry is seeded into the fixture so both legs resolve the same one; without it this cell's refusal-text truth cannot pass, so this is proven by that truth passing

the seeded-mutation negative control is per-scenario: each scenario declares the store it reads, the control perturbs THAT store, and a scenario registered with no mutation target is REFUSED at registration
the arm supports per-scenario seeding on the cloned fixture, proven by one scenario whose assertion depends on a row `--generate` never produces

deny-by-default volatile-field list with per-field shape assertions
generic --cmd-check arm with argv scenarios, tree diff, and per-scenario negative control
RunResult carries stderr; run_status generalized to arbitrary argv
per-scenario mutation target replacing the state.json-phase-only flip
command registry seeded so both legs resolve the same one

key_links: rpl-2..rpl-8 each register their group behind this seam and add scenarios to --cmd-check
rpl-3's JS-regex-literal refusal text and rpl-7's fail-open warning are stderr-only and depend on obligation (a)
every write-verb cell (rpl-3..rpl-8) depends on obligation (b): without shape assertions their tree diffs prove nothing
differ::diff_legs and the exclusion list at bee-parity/src/differ.rs:17-28 are reused unchanged
prohibitions: No edits to .bee/bin/ or packages/bee/ (D1 freeze)
No wiring flip -- nothing in .codex/hooks.json or .claude/settings.json changes
No masking a volatile field without also asserting its shape
No widening the volatile-field mask to make a red go away
Tests never touch the live .bee/ store
No ledger group logic in this cell
No scenario registered without a declared mutation target
No hand-authored BASELINE store — per-scenario seeding rides on top of `--generate`, it does not replace it

trace.outcome: Group/verb dispatch seam in queen-bee + generic bee-parity --cmd-check arm. Dispatch: crates/queen-bee/src/dispatch.rs ports bee.mjs main()s argv path (splitCommandTokens, resolveCommand, parseFlags/FLAG_ALONE_BOOLEANS, nearest-match, group usage fallbacks, emit/emitError channel split, --help and group-scoped --help) over a registration table; landing a group is ONE line in crates/queen-bee/src/groups.rs and main.rs never changes again. Unknown-flag and missing-required-flag refusal text is built from the REGISTRY entrys parameters.properties (bee.mjs:7186-7188), not from validate-args.mjs which disclaims that job, and is proven byte-identical by live --cmd-check scenarios. Parity: --cmd-check runs arbitrary argv through both runtimes over clones of one queen-bench --generate fixture, diffing stdout, STDERR, exit and store tree. All four review/advisor obligations landed: --group <name> exits non-zero on zero registered scenarios and prints per-group counts; the command registry bridge is seeded into the fixture so both legs resolve the SAME registry; the negative control is per-scenario with a declared store and a declared channel, and registration REFUSES a scenario with no mutation target; per-scenario seeding on the clone is supported and used. normalize.rs is now key-gated AND shape-gated deny-by-default: nothing is masked unless its key is named AND its value matches the declared mjs shape (toISOString 3-digit-ms Z, UUID-v4), so a chrono RFC3339 variant or a non-v4 id survives into the diff. Found and fixed a real parity bug on the way: queen-bee emitted integer-like object keys in insertion order where JSON.stringify hoists them ascending — proven red on the real binaries, fixed via crates/queen-bee/src/jsonout.rs.
deviations: AUTO-FIX (deviation rule 1, bug found in touched code): queen-bee's JSON stdout emitter diverged from the frozen mjs oracle on integer-like object keys. `JSON.stringify` enumerates array-index keys ascending BEFORE every string key (ECMA-262 OrdinaryOwnPropertyKeys); serde_json with preserve_order emits insertion order. Measured red on the real binaries via the new seam/numeric-string-keys scenario, then fixed by routing every queen-bee JSON payload through the new crates/queen-bee/src/jsonout.rs. This was in scope because obligation (c) demands the two runtimes agree on numeric-string keys, and because the seam owns the shared output emission every later ledger cell inherits.

REFUTED the cell's alternative escape for obligation (c). The cell allowed 'record that no ledger object can carry such keys, with the evidence'. The evidence says the opposite: `bee reviews record --kind manifest|preflight|decision|finding|uat` writes caller-supplied JSON into .bee/reviews/<id>.json with NO key sanitization (packages/bee/lib/reviews.mjs:283-327 via bee.mjs:4315-4322 and :4398-4404), so a numeric-string key is reachable in a real ledger store. Settled by the passing scenario instead, which is the option the cell preferred.

ADDED (deviation rule 2, missing functionality the outcome depends on): a declared, shape-asserted stderr normalization for the mjs `[bee] <cmd> <n>ms` work-visibility line (bee.mjs:7246). stderr could not be diffed at all without accounting for it, and 'ignore anything starting with [bee]' would have been exactly the blanket mask obligation (b) forbids. It is asserted in both directions instead: the mjs leg must carry exactly one well-shaped line, the queen-bee leg must carry none.

SCOPED DIVERGENCE, documented in crates/queen-bee/src/dispatch.rs: manifest drift (bee.mjs:7053 checkManifestDrift) is not ported. It is a stderr-only advisory that fires only when a PRIOR .bee/cache/manifest-hash.json disagrees; every parity leg runs once against a fresh clone that has none, so the mjs leg never emits it either.

SCOPED DIVERGENCE, documented: a registry-known command with no registered Rust handler, and a stale registry snapshot, are both REFUSED with a queen-bee-specific stderr message rather than answered with an mjs-shaped output. Impersonating mjs for an unported verb is the one failure mode that would make a parity green meaningless.
